key_insight: HVOF-applied Ni-20Cr+40TiC produced the best oxidation protection on SA516 boiler steel by forming a dense, stable oxide scale that strongly limited mass gain at 900°C.
engineering_relevance: For high-temperature boiler or thermal-processing components, the coating choice and spray process can materially improve oxidation life and reduce spallation-driven failure.
method: Compared uncoated SA516 with Ni-20Cr, Ni-20Cr+40TiC, and Ni-20Cr+40TiN coatings.
Applied coatings using High Velocity Oxygen Fuel (HVOF) and plasma spray (PS) techniques.
Ran cyclic air oxidation for 50 cycles at 900°C and analyzed phases/microstructure by XRD, SEM/EDS, and X-ray mapping.
evidence_signal: The HVOF Ni-20Cr+40TiC coating reduced maximum weight gain by 95.71% versus bare SA516, with oxide products including Cr2O3, TiO2, NiTiO4, and NiO.
watch_item: Results are based on laboratory cyclic oxidation at 900°C, so long-term service behavior under real boiler loads, thermal shocks, and erosion was not directly validated.
paper_title: Microstructure and High-Temperature Oxidation Behaviour of HVOF and Plasma Sprayed Ni–Cr-Based Ceramic Coatings on SA516 Boiler Steel
